## TL;DR

A finished close-out gate no longer aborts because another live task's markdown is dirty on `main`. Publish now treats `work/<id>-*.md` as server-owned bookkeeping: it checkpoint-commits untouched task files, and stashes/reapplies the ones the merge actually overwrites. The enqueue guard (`POST /api/tasks/:id/done`, `repoos done`, approval policy) and the `main-clean` landing check apply the same split, so a live task file no longer stops Move to done before the gate either. Dirty source files, `repoos.toml`, reports, reminders, schedules and inputs still block. New non-task paths that appear during publish preparation get three short bounded rechecks and a named failure rather than an unexplained abort.

## Work and rationale

The reported failure was in `publishCandidate` in `src/server/integration-orchestrator.ts`: `mainDirtyFilesForCloseOut` listed two live task files, neither in `overwrittenByMerge`, and the `untouchedDirty` classifier only accepted inputs/stories/reminders/schedules plus `repoos.toml`. Task markdown fell into the "so the merge would abort" branch even though `git merge` would have left those files alone. That cost #1004 a full 1,425-second gate.

I added two pure helpers in `src/core/git.ts`:

- `isTaskMarkdownBookkeepingPath(path, workDir)` — `work/*.md`, excluding `work/reports/`.
- `blockingMainDirtyPaths(paths, dirs)` — everything except that class.

`evaluateMainCleanCheck` in `src/core/landable.ts` now takes the branch's changed paths and reports a dirty live task file as a **warning** when the branch does not change it, while a task file the branch itself modifies, any source/config path, report, reminder, schedule or input still fails. `gatherApprovalPreflight` bases its boolean `mainDirty` on the blocking subset while keeping the raw list for the checklist. The done route and `enqueueCloseOutForTask` use `blockingMainDirtyPaths` before deciding to return 409/stop.

In publish, I extracted `settlePublishDirty`. It reads the dirty set, computes `overwrittenByMerge` (unchanged `#0820` merge-tree logic), then re-reads up to three times. New task markdown is folded into the set and logged; new non-task paths get 150–450 ms of grace, are logged, and are then reported as blockers. The untouched classifier now accepts task markdown, and the checkpoint commit retries on transient `index.lock` failures. A task file in the overwritten set still goes through the existing stash/pop path, so both the branch change and the local edit survive.

Tests were added or updated in `done-guard-orchestrator.test.ts`, `done-guard.test.ts`, `git-worktree.test.ts` and `landable.test.ts`, including the primary dirty-live-task case, the mid-preparation task-file case, the mid-preparation source-file refusal, and the dirty-file-the-merge-touches stash case. `docs/close-out-pipeline.md` updates the `main-clean` row, the publish section and the `--commit-dirty` guidance.

## Approaches tried

I considered omitting dirty task files from `mainDirtyFilesForCloseOut` outright. That would make every consumer agree, but it also hides the files from the overwrite analysis, so a merge that genuinely touches one would hit git's raw failure at the end of the gate. Keeping the raw list and filtering at each decision point was more code but preserves the overwrite safety and the useful "which files are dirty" detail.

I also considered refusing all mid-preparation task-file changes (the old behaviour). That leaves the same bug class in a narrower window: a live writer can dirty a task file during the merge-tree call on a busy board. Since checkpointing preserves every byte, I extended the tolerance and updated the old human-task-edit test to assert the edit is committed, not lost.

## Challenges and blockers

The existing watchdog-delta filter removes some task files before publish, so tests had to seed ordinary (non-watchdog) task content. The mid-preparation tests also needed an already-dirty file so the merge-tree spy would actually run; without it the test's write arrived after the analysis and proved nothing.

No human-only step was required. No external device, account or network measurement was used.

## Key learnings

The close-out has several independent dirty-main gates (enqueue, approval preflight, landing checklist, publish), so fixing only publish would still leave Move to done blocked or the checklist red. The ownership split has to be shared. Also, "dirty file the merge touches" is already handled by stash/pop, so the correct narrow fix is to checkpoint untouched task bookkeeping and leave the overwritten set on the existing path.
